original_question: Prove that for every generalized minimal flow u(x,t), the vorticity level sets curl u(x,t)=const are real-analytic curves.
target_in_paper: Section 6.3, Problem 14: the analyticity of vorticity level lines for generalized minimal flows (GM-flows).
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right topic: the paper's open problem about generalized minimal flows in 2D Euler dynamics and the claim that the vorticity contours should be real-analytic. It is also close in wording to the paper's official formulation.
missing_details: The ambient setting is omitted: the paper works on a compact analytic Riemannian 2-manifold M, possibly with boundary, in Section 6.3.
The relevant function space is not stated: YU(M) is the Yudovich space of divergence-free vector fields u on M with curl u in L∞(M).
The term 'generalized minimal flow' is not defined. In the paper, u is a GM-flow if for every w in the weak H^1-closure of its Euler orbit O(u), one has ||curl w||L2 = ||curl u||L2.

The Euler dynamics and orbit notation are implicit in the draft. In the paper, S_t: YU(M) → YU(M) is the Euler evolution, O(u) is the orbit, and the GM condition is defined through that orbit closure.
The quantifiers should be explicit: the statement is meant for every time t along the Euler evolution and for every vorticity value c.

The paper says 'level lines,' not full 'level sets.' This matters because Problem 15 separately suggests the existence of a background region B0 on which curl u is constant, so a full level set need not be only a curve.
The paper's motivation mentions periodic or quasiperiodic GM-flows, but Problem 14 itself is stated for any GM-flow, not only for those special cases.

The meaning of 'real-analytic' should be tied to the analytic structure of the surface M: the intended objects are real-analytic curves in the analytic 2-manifold, not merely smooth curves or analyticity in time.
refined_question: Let M be a compact real-analytic Riemannian 2-manifold, possibly with boundary, and let YU(M) be the Yudovich space of divergence-free vector fields u on M such that curl u ∈ L∞(M). Let S_t denote the 2D Euler evolution on YU(M), let O(u0) be the orbit of u0 under S_t, and let O(u0)¯ be its weak H^1-closure. Assume that u0 ∈ YU(M) is a generalized minimal flow in the sense that ||curl w||L2(M) = ||curl u0||L2(M) for every w ∈ O(u0)¯. If u(t) = S_tu0, prove that for every t and every c ∈ R, each vorticity level line of ω(t, x) = curl u(t, x), i.e. each connected one-dimensional component of {x ∈ M : ω(t, x) = c}, is a real-analytic curve in M.
justification: The draft is targeting Section 6.3, Problem 14 almost verbatim. The surrounding setup in the paper defines the ambient manifold M, the Yudovich space YU(M), the Euler flow S_t, orbit closure, and the precise definition of a GM-flow in Definition 6.7. The nearby discussion explains why the problem is being asked: stationary flows already have real-analytic vorticity level lines, and the authors conjecture the same for nonstationary GM-flows, motivated especially by periodic or quasiperiodic examples. The draft's main inaccuracy is the phrase 'level sets ... are real-analytic curves': the paper asks about level lines, and Problem 15 separately indicates that a full level set may also contain an entire background region B0 where the vorticity is constant. So the refined question keeps the exact GM/Yudovich setup and narrows the claim to one-dimensional level-line components, which is the closest stand-alone version faithful to Problem 14.
